text:
alex: Hey folks, apply for the us-west GPU pool just failed and now the terraform backend lock looks stuck on the Azure blob lease. apply -> error: state locked by lease id 3f2a...

miriam: ugh. which backend are we using? blob + lease table or v2?

alex: storage account `redwood-tfstate-prod`, container `tfstate`, file `eng/compute/gpu-pools.tfstate`. Using blob lease (we migrated from S3 last quarter).

jamal: did `terraform force-unlock` complain?

alex: yes. force-unlock returns success locally but the blob lease still shows as active when I run `az storage blob lease show` -> shows lease state = locked, lease status = leased. azure CLI's lease break command isn't releasing it.

taylor: devops-bot triggered an automatic retry which made it worse, two applies started concurrently before the lease finally held. we need a safe recovery plan, don't run more applies. :grimacing:

devops-bot: autoscaler: noticed drift in gpu-pool count during retries, pausing cluster autoscaling to avoid over-provisioning.

miriam: ok let's avoid a double create/destroy. checklist: 1) stop any automated CI runs, 2) verify no in-flight terraform apply in CI, 3) snapshot the current blob object, 4) break the lease from Azure control plane if possible, 5) if not, create a temporary state copy and import resources to it before proceeding.

alex: I took a copy: `az storage blob download --container-name tfstate --name eng/compute/gpu-pools.tfstate --file /tmp/gpu-pools.tfstate.snapshot`

jamal: good. if lease won't break we can perform a coordinated state split: create a new state file `eng/compute/gpu-pools-recovery.tfstate`, then `terraform state pull` -> edit? careful: editing state json is risky. prefer `terraform state mv` to move resources into the recovery state.

taylor: steps I suggest (manual, one operator):
1) stop CI and add a repo-wide lock file so nobody triggers runs.
2) from a machine with az login, attempt `az storage blob lease break --container-name tfstate --name eng/compute/gpu-pools.tfstate --lease-break-period 60`
3) if it succeeds, run `terraform force-unlock <lease-id>` and re-run `terraform plan`
4) if it fails, create a new backend config pointing to `eng/compute/gpu-pools-recovery.tfstate` (a new blob). run `terraform init -backend-config='key=eng/compute/gpu-pools-recovery.tfstate'`
5) run `terraform state list` against the old snapshot and `terraform import` resources into the recovery state, or use `terraform state mv -state=old.tfstate -state-out=recovery.tfstate`

miriam: small detail: terraform state mv supports `-state` and `-state-out` for local files, but with remote blob backends you need to pull both states locally first: `terraform state pull > old.tfstate`, then `terraform state mv -state=old.tfstate -state-out=recovery.tfstate module.gpu_pool.aws_autoscaling_group.example module.gpu_pool.aws_autoscaling_group.example`. then push `recovery.tfstate` back to blob.

alex: thanks. I also tried `az storage blob lease renew` and got 409 conflict. That suggests the lease owner is some long-running process (CI container) that didn't die cleanly.

jamal: we should kill any orphaned runners. I'll check GitHub Actions / our self-hosted fleet for any live terraform containers hitting the backend.

devops-bot: infra-alert: Found 2 self-hosted runners with active terraform processes (runner-12, runner-07). Recommending lockdown.

taylor: if we end up doing the recovery-state route, we must coordinate a canary apply with `-target` on the most idempotent resources first (security groups, subnets), then do full apply once confident. Also open a short maintenance window in #general.

miriam: agree. also add this as a follow-up: consider moving to a small DynamoDB-style lease table for locking (or use backend that supports atomic leases) instead of relying on blob lease behavior across regions. Blob leases are finnicky with eventual consistency.

alex: action items: jamal -> kill orphaned runners (in progress). taylor -> prepare recovery backend config and a script to pull & mv state locally. miriam -> coordinate maintenance window and CI pause. I'll hold any manual applies until we confirm recovery.

jamal: killed runners, no active terraform processes now.

alex: did a quick test: `az storage blob lease break` returned success after runner kill. lease state now: broken.

taylor: cool. next: run `terraform init -reconfigure -backend-config='key=eng/compute/gpu-pools.tfstate'` then `terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan`. Do not `apply` yet. post plan here.

alex: plan looks sane, small change to tags on ASG, no destructive changes. I'll wait for :thumbsup: from miriam and jamal then apply.

miriam: :thumbsup: go ahead in 15m, I'll monitor and hold pager.

alex: applied successfully. cluster returned to normal, autoscaler resumed.

taylor: follow-up ticket: switch lock method, add a non-destructive test that verifies lease break semantics after CI cancellation. also document recovery runbook for blob-lease stuck cases.

miriam: filed INFRA-4827 with the runbook and migration proposal. thanks team. :tada:
